_doc: Single source of truth for the nexys_rv32 SoC. Edit this file, then run: py tools/gen_all.py. Every derived file (Verilog header, C header, linker scripts, docs tables, XDC clock) is regenerated from it.

clock._doc: CPU clock. 100000000 uses the oscillator directly. Any other value instantiates an MMCM in fpga/rtl/fpga_top.v (supported: 50000000, 75000000).

core._doc: default_core selects the core in the FPGA build and in run_sim.py default runs: 'pipe' (5-stage) or 'mc' (multi-cycle).

sim._doc: Simulation-only settings. compliance_ram_size is the RAM size of the riscv-arch-test configuration: its branch/jump tests are up to 1.75 MB, larger than any on-chip RAM, so those runs use a bigger simulated RAM (same base address, same decode rules).

timer._doc: mtime increments at tick_hz. 1 MHz gives microseconds in software.

seg7._doc: Each of the 8 digits is lit for 1/digit_hz s; full refresh = digit_hz/8 Hz (manual: 1 to 16 ms per full refresh).

regs: Write a byte to transmit (bits 7:0). Ignored while STATUS.TX_BUSY=1.
bit0 TX_BUSY, bit1 RX_VALID, bit2 RX_OVERRUN (write 1 to clear), bit3 RX_FRAME_ERR (write 1 to clear)
Debounced buttons: bit0 BTNC, bit1 BTNU, bit2 BTNL, bit3 BTNR, bit4 BTND; 1 = pressed
Sticky press events, same bit order as BUTTONS; write 1 to clear
32-bit value shown as 8 hex digits; digit 7 (left) = bits 31:28
bit n lights the decimal point of digit n
Test result mailbox: 1 = pass, (n<<1)|1 = fail with code n. The simulation testbench stops on a write; in hardware it is a plain register.
Upper word of the riscv-tests tohost doubleword; scratch
bit0 zicsr, bit1 timer_irq, bit2 zifencei, bit3 core is pipelined

csr._doc: Machine-mode CSRs implemented when features.zicsr=1. Any other CSR address raises an illegal-instruction exception.
list: MTIP (bit 7) from the timer; writes ignored
